name: PaintClarity
author: paintops

sections.description:
PaintClarity turns your WordPress site into the back office for your painting business. (PaintClarity was formerly known as PaintOps. Same plugin, same team, same data.) Build professional quotes, send them to customers who can view, e-sign, and pay a deposit online, schedule crews on a calendar, track every job from lead to invoice, and, on Pro, see your real profit per job, per crew, and per worker.

It was built by a painter, for painters. The quote builder understands painting scope: interior/exterior components, standard inclusions and exclusions, and the disclaimer language that keeps you out of disputes. Your data lives in your own WordPress database, not locked inside someone else’s SaaS.

Quote to invoice, start to finish

  • Quotes, estimates & bids: a scope-aware builder with reusable inclusions/exclusions, itemized or lump-sum pricing, printable output, and email delivery.
  • A professional customer page: your customer opens a clean, branded page (your logo, your terms & conditions) and accepts by typing their name, an e-signature-grade record with timestamp. They can also decline with a reason, or ask a question, and you’re notified either way.
  • Acceptance converts the quote to a job automatically, whether they paid a deposit online or you shook hands, and a “Mark as Won” button covers the phone call.
  • Invoices: numbered invoices for the balance (full or partial), emailed or shared by link, payable online (Pro + Stripe) or marked paid for check/cash, with the payment logged so balances always agree.
  • Receivables at a glance: unpaid invoices surface on your dashboard with amounts and age.

Running the work

  • Scheduling calendar with crew filtering, worker badges, time-off, and a subscribe link for Google/Apple/Outlook. Add your own recurring holiday labels.
  • Crews: group your painters into named, colored crews; staff a job with one tap and filter the calendar and reports by crew.
  • Job board / pipeline: Quote → Active → Completed, plus a lost-leads drawer with the customer’s decline reason so you can revive the ones worth re-working.
  • A real app for your painters: install-to-home-screen (PWA), a “My Jobs” home, one-tap directions (Google/Apple/Waze), per-job check-in/out that works offline and syncs, photo/receipt/note logging, a “My Hours” view of their own time and pay, and a “Mark Job Complete” button that notifies the office. Workers see only what their permissions allow, never your numbers.
  • Customers: a directory with contact details, lifetime value, job history, and multiple service addresses per customer, built for landlords, realtors, property managers, and GCs whose one account means a dozen properties.
  • Before/After photos with camera alignment overlay and a compare slider.
  • Color Visualizer: load a photo of the house or the room, select the surface, and turn a color wheel until it is the color you are proposing. The wall changes color and keeps its own shading, grain and texture. Select by fill, by matching color, or by dragging a box over a big flat wall. Handles stucco, siding, brick, concrete block and interior drywall, takes the Sherwin-Williams or Benjamin Moore number alongside it, and prints or saves the render for the customer. The Manual tab runs entirely in your browser: no photo is uploaded anywhere.
  • AI Visualizer (Pro): the other tab. Upload or take a photo, pick colors by brand and name from the Sherwin-Williams and Benjamin Moore books, add a note like “paint the stone wall too, in Alabaster”, and get back a realistic repainted photo to show the customer. This tab sends the photo to OpenAI under your own API key (Settings > AI), billed to your OpenAI account at a few cents per render. Renders can be saved to the job’s photos. Colors on screen are approximate; brand and color names are trademarks of their owners and PaintClarity is not affiliated with any paint manufacturer.
  • Trade calculators, paint-color tracking, and resource links.
  • A choice of visual themes (light, dark, industrial, and more) with a modern app-style navigation bar on desktop and phone.

What Pro adds

  • Job financials & profitability: costs, materials, labor hours; gross, expenses, profit, and margin per job; a Profits dashboard with profit-by-classification, profit-per-hour rankings, and profit by crew and by worker (allocated by logged hours).
  • Expenses & receipts against any job, plus business-level and vehicle expense tracking for tax time.
  • Online payments: deposits on quote acceptance and invoice balances through Stripe Checkout, recorded automatically.
  • AI tools (bring your own OpenAI key): estimate dimensions, gallons, and a Description of Work from a photo; scan receipts to auto-fill expenses; get feedback on or a rewrite of your quote wording.

Pro is a paid upgrade handled through Freemius. The free plugin is fully functional on its own; Pro is optional.

Bundled artwork

The four ready-made logos offered under Business > Logo URL (assets/img/logos/) are AI-generated original artwork created for this plugin. They carry no third-party rights and are distributed under the same GPLv2-or-later license as the rest of the plugin. They are optional, off by default, and carry no PaintClarity branding or link.

External services

This plugin can connect to the following third-party services. Some are optional and only run when you enable and configure the corresponding feature.

OpenAI (Pro AI features, optional). When you use an AI feature (Photo Estimate, Receipt Scan, Description-of-Work Feedback or Rewrite), the plugin sends the relevant input, the photo you choose to upload and/or the quote text you are working on, to the OpenAI API using your own OpenAI API key, and receives the generated result. No data is sent unless you click one of these buttons. PaintClarity does not store the photo. Requests go to https://api.openai.com. See OpenAI’s Terms (https://openai.com/policies/terms-of-use) and Privacy Policy (https://openai.com/policies/privacy-policy).

Stripe (Pro online payments, optional). If you enable card payments and a customer pays online, the plugin creates a Stripe Checkout session and verifies Stripe’s webhook using your own Stripe keys. Order/amount details are exchanged with Stripe to process the payment. Requests go to https://api.stripe.com. See Stripe’s Services Agreement (https://stripe.com/legal/ssa) and Privacy Policy (https://stripe.com/privacy).

Google Maps Platform (optional). If you add a Google Maps API key, address fields use Google Places/Geocoding for autocomplete and validation, and job locations may be shown on an embedded map. The address text you type is sent to Google to return suggestions. Requests go to https://maps.googleapis.com and related Google Maps endpoints. See Google’s Terms (https://cloud.google.com/maps-platform/terms) and Privacy Policy (https://policies.google.com/privacy). (One-tap turn-by-turn Directions for your crew use keyless map links and need no API key.)

YouTube and Vimeo (Resources page video embeds, optional). The Resources page (staff-facing, inside your admin area) lets you save links to training videos, and seeds a starter list of publicly available painting tutorials on YouTube. When a staff member clicks a saved YouTube or Vimeo link’s play button, the video is embedded on the page via the provider’s standard embed player (www.youtube.com / player.vimeo.com), which loads content from that provider and is subject to its terms; no data is sent until the play button is clicked, and you can delete any or all saved links. See YouTube’s Terms (https://www.youtube.com/t/terms) and Google’s Privacy Policy (https://policies.google.com/privacy), and Vimeo’s Terms (https://vimeo.com/terms) and Privacy Policy (https://vimeo.com/privacy).

Freemius (licensing & updates). PaintClarity uses the Freemius SDK to manage Pro licenses, deliver Pro updates, and (optionally) collect anonymous usage diagnostics you can opt out of. Site and license information is exchanged with Freemius. See Freemius’s Terms (https://freemius.com/terms/) and Privacy Policy (https://freemius.com/privacy/).

You control every one of these by whether you enter the corresponding API key and enable the feature. With no keys entered, PaintClarity runs entirely on your own site.

Privacy

Your customers’ details live in your own WordPress database. PaintClarity’s author never sees them, and nothing is sent to a PaintClarity server. That also means you, not the plugin, are the one a customer asks when they want to know what you hold about them, so the plugin’s job is to make sure you can answer.

Quote and invoice pages are blocked from search engines. Those pages are reached by a long private link rather than a password, and a link can be forwarded, pasted into a chat, or picked up from a referrer header. Every customer-facing document PaintClarity serves is marked no-index, no-archive at both the page and the header level, so a link that escapes cannot turn into a search result.

Data requests work out of the box. Under Tools -> Export Personal Data and Tools -> Erase Personal Data, WordPress can search PaintClarity by email address. Export collects the customer record, their jobs, quotes, invoices, payments, and the emails you sent them. Erase removes their details from all of it.

Erasing does not destroy your books. Quotes, invoices and payments are kept and stripped of the name, address, phone, email, typed signature and IP address instead of being deleted, because a business is required to keep financial records for years and data protection law allows exactly that. Any quote or invoice link previously sent to that customer stops working. Job photos are left for you to review yourself rather than deleted automatically.

Suggested privacy policy wording for what PaintClarity stores and which services can receive data is added to Settings -> Privacy -> Policy Guide.

Three optional limits, all off by default, under PaintClarity -> Settings -> Privacy & Customer Data: delete the emailed-communication log after N months, forget the IP address recorded when a quote was signed online after N months, and make quote and invoice links stop working after N days. A business working only in the United States can leave all three off and nothing changes.

None of this is Pro. It is all in the free plugin.
sections.installation:
1. Install PaintClarity from the Plugins screen (Plugins → Add New → search “PaintClarity”), or upload the plugin ZIP under Plugins → Add New → Upload Plugin. Activate it.
  2. Create a WordPress Page and add the shortcode [paintops_app]. This one page is your whole PaintClarity app; it routes internally.
  3. Go to PaintClarity → Settings and set your Company Profile (business name, logo, country, currency), and review the Setup Health panel.
  4. (Optional) Add team members under PaintClarity → Painters/Helpers, set their permissions, and group them into Crews.
  5. (Optional) Add your Quote Terms & Conditions under Business Settings so customers see and sign against them.
  6. (Optional, Pro) Under Settings → AI Settings connect OpenAI, under Stripe Payments add your Stripe secret key AND webhook signing secret (both are required before online payment buttons appear), and add a Google Maps API key for address autocomplete.
sections.faq:
Do I need a paid account to use it?

No. The free plugin runs entirely on your own WordPress site and lets you quote, schedule, and manage unlimited jobs. Pro is an optional upgrade.

What happens to my data if I deactivate or delete the plugin?

Nothing is deleted. Your jobs, quotes, customers, payments, hours, and photos stay in your WordPress database, so nothing is lost if you deactivate temporarily or reinstall later. If you truly want the data gone, delete the plugin’s tables and its uploads from your database and media library.

Does it work without OpenAI, Stripe, or Google Maps?

Yes. Those are optional integrations. If you don’t enter their keys, the related features simply stay off and everything else works, including keyless turn-by-turn directions for your crew.

Can my customers really sign a quote online?

They accept by typing their full name, which is stored with a timestamp and IP address alongside your Terms & Conditions, a solid acceptance record. They can also decline with a reason, and change their minds later.

Who pays for the AI usage?

You do, through your own OpenAI account and key, typically a fraction of a cent to a few cents per action. PaintClarity adds per-month usage caps you control so costs stay predictable.

Can my painters log in without seeing my numbers?

Yes. Painters/Helpers get a dedicated role with opt-in permissions and their own app view: My Jobs, My Hours (their own time and pay only), directions, check-in/out, photos and receipts. Financial figures are owner-level and hidden from workers unless you explicitly grant access.

Does it work in the field with bad reception?

The app installs to a phone’s home screen, and Time Clock check-in/out keeps working offline and syncs when a connection returns.

Where is my data stored?

In your own WordPress database. PaintClarity doesn’t host your business data on an external server.
sections.changelog:
1.2.075

  • Fixed: the Resources list’s stylesheet and script loaded on every page of the site and every wp-admin screen, whether or not a resource list was on it. They now load only where a list renders (the app’s Resources page and pages using the [paintops_resources] shortcode). The small Pro-unlicensed upgrade-button script was scoped the same way. Ordinary pages of the site carry no PaintClarity assets at all.
  • Changed: the PaintClarity app page is no longer added to a menu that has “Automatically add new top-level pages” turned on, and it stays out of a theme’s automatic page lists (the no-menu fallback and the Page List block). It still shows under Pages and in the menu editor, so adding it to a menu on purpose works as before.

1.2.074

  • Added: Business Notes has an “Add a Note to a Job” accordion. Pick an open request or job, write the note, and it lands on that job’s Notes & Photos log with the time and your name, without leaving the page.
  • Added: “Preview Online Quote” on the quote screen opens the page the customer will see, in a new tab. Opening it while logged in as staff never counts as a customer view: no “Viewed by customer” badge, no owner notification, no history line, and the quote is not marked sent.
  • Changed: on the Free plan the Visualizer opens on the Manual tab, where the working tool is. The AI tab is still one tap away with its upgrade details. Pro is unchanged.

1.2.073

  • Changed: the crew initials on a Jobs row are the whole control; the “Show names” / “Hide names” text is gone. Click or tap the initials to list the full names, again, outside, or Escape to collapse. Screen readers hear “Show crew names” / “Hide crew names”.

1.2.072

  • Improved: one name for new work. The Jobs page button reads “+ New”, and the menu item, the New Customer page buttons and the form heading all read “New Request / Job”. The Quote / Estimate / Bid / Job pills and the remembered choice are unchanged.
  • Fixed: after creating a job the cleared form still carried the paintable square feet and the “Exclude this job from financial reports” box. Both now clear, with the exclusion back to off.
  • Improved: crew names on a Jobs row. The initials sit in a plain control with a “Show names” label beside them; a click, tap, Enter or Space lists every crew member’s full name on its own line underneath and the label reads “Hide names”. Clicking again or outside collapses it. Hover titles on desktop stay, and the row’s Actions menu and links are untouched.
  • Improved: the amount column on the owner’s Jobs rows is labeled “Job Value”. The painter view is unchanged.

1.2.071

  • Fixed: on the quote screen, pressing “Save … as this job’s paintable area” re-rendered the calculator from its starter values (1,500 sq ft, 600 ft of baseboard) while still showing them as results, so a room entered as 224 sq ft with no baseboards offered Interior Painting at 1,239 sq ft and $1,290 of baseboards to the quote. The typed values now survive that press.
  • Changed: each calculator’s green button adds only that calculator’s numbers to the quote (“Add These Numbers to Quote”). It used to add every calculator on the page at once, including one calculated earlier with its starter values and never touched again.
  • Fixed: Job Pulse compared payroll with the “labor rate” setting divided by this job’s observed hours per day, which on a short day turned a $575 day into $172.50 an hour and reported more “charged” than the whole job. It now holds payroll against the quote’s own labor line; when the quote has none, the setting is named as a suggestion, per standard day, never as what the quote charged. Settings calls it “Suggested labor cost” throughout.
  • Fixed: on Profits, “Profit By Job Classification” and “Profit by Crew / Worker” covered every job ever, including upcoming and Not Won, under a “year to date” heading. They now cover the same jobs as the year’s totals (that year, started, not Not Won) and say so.
  • Improved: the Profits year block says how many jobs have no hours or expenses logged yet and how much of their revenue is counted as profit only because no costs are on the books.
  • New: the manual Visualizer tab offers the job’s existing photos as thumbnails, the same strip the AI tab has, so an original never has to be uploaded twice; the job stays attached when switching tabs. Thumbnails on both tabs carry a caption (the photo’s note, or Before / After / Photo with the day and time).
  • New: on the manual Visualizer, a “Next tap on the photo” switch (New surface, Add to it, Take away) replaces having to know Shift-click and Alt-drag, so a selection that spread onto the floor can be corrected by touch. Undo now reverses the last tap rather than removing the whole surface.
  • Changed: colors spotted in the AI Visualizer notes are shown as suggestions with an “Add to a surface” action, and only colors on a surface reach the render. A sentence that says what to keep, leave or not paint is never read as a color to use, and a plain color word such as “white” is not matched to a catalog color unless its brand or code is beside it.
  • Fixed: after saving an AI preview to a job, “Open job photos” pointed at a WordPress admin address; it now opens the job’s Notes & Photos inside the app.
  • Improved: Before / After pairing on Notes & Photos picks from thumbnails with captions and ids instead of “Photo #12, timestamp” dropdowns, so two photos from the same minute can be told apart.
  • Improved: a Cloudflare Turnstile key pair that cannot work now shows on the Quote Request Form summary line (“Turnstile NOT WORKING, requests filed under Spam”) and as its own row on the Setup Health board, instead of only inside the section. Saving a bad pair has been refused since 1.2.066.
  • Fixed: the Appearance summary line described the app bar and mobile display while the sidebar layout was on, which replaces both. It now states the effective layout, and the overridden controls say “Not in effect”.
  • Fixed: a job marked completed before its scheduled start still showed “Arrive in N days” on the job page. A completed job shows “Completed “.
  • Improved: more than 16 hours for one person on one date (usually a double entry) is called out on Job Pulse and badged on the job’s Hours page and on the Financials hours editor, rather than carried into the per-day figures without comment.
  • Fixed: a whole-dollar total that the arithmetic left a hair under the whole number (14,689.999…) printed as $14,690.00 on the dashboard tiles, where cents are shown only when there are cents.

1.2.070

  • Improved: the Jobs page reads the same in row view and board view. The row view’s “Quotes Out” is now “Requests”, matching the board’s first column, and a collapsed “Completed” section joins it below Upcoming, with the same count and the same “N unpaid, $X outstanding” note the board shows. Finished jobs with a balance read “Balance due” with a Collect link; the Actions menu offers the same moves as the board.
  • Improved: Production Rates shows each job’s Started date instead of Completed. A scheduled job always has a start date, while the completed date is only stamped by Mark Completed, so most rows read “No date”.
  • Fixed: a job marked “exclude from financial reports” was left off the Production Rates list. That flag is about money; a production rate is hours over area, so every completed job now counts.
  • Fixed: in the sidebar layout, hovering WP Admin or Sign out turned the text dark against the dark rail; a theme’s own link hover was winning.
  • Removed: the “Waiting on payment” list on the Jobs row view. The Completed section now carries the unpaid count and total with a Collect link per job, and Needs Your Attention lists the same balances with Mark As Paid and Record Payment, so a third list with no actions was clutter.

1.2.069

  • Fixed: the last wide accent bars are gone: the Business Checkup summary box, Job Pulse tiles, calendar entries, the form section labels, the About panel on Business, the admin-only note above the profit summary and the vivid theme’s extra-wide label edge. Where a colour carried meaning (red for attention, green for clean, tile tone) it now colours the box’s regular 1px border instead.

1.2.068

  • Fixed: AI Visualizer renders came back zoomed in, with the ceiling and floor cut off. The photo is fitted to the model’s frame by extending its edges; the flat grey bars used for that read as letterboxing to the model, which zoomed the photo to fill them. The extension is now a mirrored copy of the photo’s own edges, so there is nothing to fill in and the render lands back on the real photo.
  • Fixed: the render on the right showed larger than the photo on the left. Both are now capped at the same height so they sit side by side at one size.
  • Fixed: a plugin that queues a script late in the page (an SEO toolbar, for one) could still reach the app page past the “other plugins” setting. The check now runs as each tag is printed, whenever it was queued.

1.2.067

  • New: Payments on the Free plan. Every job has a Payments page for anyone who can see money: record cash, check or in-person card payments and refunds, remove a mistake, and see Billed, Paid and Still owed. Payments recorded here flip the job’s invoices to paid when they cover the job, the same as on Pro. On Pro the Payments action opens the Financials payments drawer.
  • New: invoicing more than the job is billing now asks first. An invoice above what is left to invoice comes back as a question with the numbers; confirm it and the invoice is created and Billable on the job is raised to match, with a line in Customer History saying so.
  • New: the year-end report adds “tax to remit, by filing period”: one table per tax label and rate, by quarter, with a by-month view for monthly filers. Cash basis, following the payment date.
  • New: the quote form holds its Request a Quote button until Cloudflare Turnstile hands over a token, so a person cannot send the form before the check passes.
  • New: quote form submissions that are plainly automated (the hidden field filled in, or no Turnstile token while Turnstile is on) are dropped without creating a row. The Leads screen shows one line, “N automated submissions dropped in the last 30 days”, instead of a Spam tab full of them. Softer rejections keep their rows so Not spam stays possible.
  • New: a pattern check on the quote form for sites without Turnstile: first name equal to last name (or names with digits and underscores), a message mostly in non-Latin script on a US, CA, GB, AU, NZ or IE business, and links in the message. Two of the three together flag a request as spam; one alone never does.
  • Improved: a Financials save no longer restamps every payment with the person saving and the current time; a payment that did not change keeps who recorded it and when.
  • Improved: the AI photo estimate shows metres, square metres and litres on a business set to metric, and the write-up is asked for in metric too.
  • Fixed: the AI Visualizer’s result box scrolled under the sticky header when a render started, cutting the progress spinner in half.
  • New: other plugins’ scripts and styles stay off the app page. SEO toolbars, chat widgets, cookie banners and page-builder bundles have no job on the private app screens and can make them jump (Rank Math’s Frontend Stats Bar inserted and removed a bar on every screen). Your theme, WordPress itself and anything loaded from another site are not affected, and the rest of your site is untouched. Settings > Appearance > Navigation has the switch and an exceptions box by plugin folder.

1.2.066

  • Fixed: on the Quote Request Form settings, a browser’s password manager could fill the Cloudflare Turnstile fields with your WordPress username and password when you pressed Save, because a text field followed by a password field looks like a login form. The widget then failed on every visit and every real request was filed under Spam without a word. Secret fields across the plugin (Turnstile, Stripe, OpenAI) are now masked text fields that password managers leave alone, and a Turnstile key that is not a key is refused at save with a message naming the field.
  • Fixed: a Turnstile widget that cannot complete no longer fails silently. Two requests in a row arriving without a Turnstile token put a warning at the top of Leads and on the settings page, saying what usually causes it and how to turn Turnstile off; administrators viewing the form also see a note under the widget when Cloudflare reports it did not load. A saved key that is not a Turnstile key is called out the same way.
  • Improved: the quote form’s validation messages are plain: “Some fields are missing or need a correction” and “First name is required”, instead of “A few fields need a moment”.
  • Improved: the City, State and Zip fields on the quote form no longer show example values.
  • Improved: notices and banners across the app lose their thick left accent bar and keep an ordinary border (the same rule that took the top rule off the stat tiles).

1.2.064

  • New: Message History is now Customer History. One timeline per job, newest first: the quote request, the quote going out, opened, signed or declined, invoices raised, sent and paid, every payment and refund, the job finishing, and every call, text, email and note in between, with a funnel strip across the top that shows which stage the customer has reached and what has not happened yet. Same page, same link.
  • New: painters can reach the office from a job. Call, Text and Email pills to the company phone and email on the painter’s job page and Customer History, with the job already named, logged as “Called the office”. A contact a painter records from the field is now emailed to the office, which the form always said and never did.
  • New: the AI Visualizer can save a render when it was opened without a job: pick the job from a list. When it was opened from a job, the job’s actions bar sits above the tabs so the rest of the job is one tap away.
  • Improved: the AI Visualizer no longer comes back cropped or reframed. The model only draws on three fixed canvases, so a phone photo was being recomposed to fill one; the photo is now placed on the right canvas with flat bars, the model paints it as-is, and the bars are trimmed off the result, so the render has exactly the photo’s own edges. The model is also told not to write any text, labels or swatches into the picture, and to keep each wall one uniform color from floor to ceiling, after real renders came back with a caption strip and a lighter band under the ceiling.
  • Improved: the AI Visualizer’s result bar is Download and Save; the original photo already sits beside the result, so Hold to compare and Render again are gone, replaced by a note on how to re-render. While a render is in flight the result box itself shows Rendering with a spinner and the status, so the wait is visible without looking down at the Render button.
  • Improved: the standard mileage rate is per tax year (2025 = 70 cents, 2026 = 72.5 cents built in), each trip is valued at the rate of the year it was driven, and typing this year’s rate no longer restates last year’s report.
  • Improved: outside the US the vehicle and vendor screens stop talking about the IRS, 1099s and miles: a Canadian company sees CRA, T4A and kilometres, a British one HMRC and miles, and Colour is spelled the local way.
  • Improved: the calendar feed has an option to leave customer names, street addresses and phone numbers out, for a calendar the whole crew can see.
  • Improved: deleting a job that carries payments or paid invoices now says how much money leaves the books before you confirm.
  • Fixed: a fourth real quote request from the same address inside the window no longer lands in Spam because bot submissions were being counted toward the cap.
  • Fixed: the card processing fee and its sentence on the quote only apply where a card can actually be taken online; Free and Pro-without-Stripe sites no longer disclose a fee nobody can pay. The card fee and 1099 settings are Pro-only on the settings page.
  • Fixed: Job Pulse honours the licence, so a lapsed Pro build locks it with the rest.
  • Fixed: Profits no longer counts a job moved to Not Won, or a job whose start date is still ahead, as the year’s revenue; the Profit per Hour denominator follows the same rule.
  • Fixed: the review request greets the customer by first name; {customer_full_name} is available for the body.
  • Fixed: PHP notices on document upload, on CSV import under PHP 8.4, and when the Email Quote page is opened with a stale id (it now says the quote was not found).
  • Fixed: the AI Visualizer’s monthly cap message named the wrong feature, the renders-used line did not move until a reload, and the void-invoice prompt now says the reason is shown to the customer.
  • New: Hours on the Free plan. Every job has an Hours page (staff only): one row per person per day with a note, each row removable on its own. Hours logged on Free feed Profit per Hour and the labor lines the moment Pro is turned on, because they go in the same table with the worker’s rate stamped at save. On Pro the Hours action still opens the Financials hours editor.
  • New: quotes carry cents. A quote total, its tax and an accepted upsell are stored to the cent instead of being rounded to whole dollars, so a $1,847.50 itemized quote no longer reads $1,848 on the customer’s page and the invoice. Existing figures are untouched; the columns are widened on upgrade.
  • New: a printable letterhead on the quote. The company name, address, phone and email print across the top of the customer’s quote and the printable version, only the lines you have filled in.
  • New: a subcontractor pay run on the Business page. Pick a through date and the date you paid, and every unpaid subcontractor hour up to that date is stamped with the pay date. The year report and the vendor report then follow the money: labor counts in the year it was paid (cash basis, what the 1099 or T4A asks for), with hours that have no pay date yet shown by work date and called out as such.
  • New: payee details per vendor and subcontractor (legal name, entity type, address, last four of the tax id, how they are paid) on the Business page, carried onto the vendor report and its CSV, so the January forms can be filled from one screen.
  • Improved: money on the dashboards drops the “.00” (a $1,800 job reads $1,800, a $1,847.50 one keeps its cents) on the Profits tiles, the rankings cards, the Financials summary and the Waiting on payment drawer. Lists, invoices and anything a customer sees keep two decimals.
  • Improved: one date format everywhere. Every date the app shows follows the site’s Settings > General date and time format instead of three different built-in styles.
  • Improved: the dark theme covers the classic layout as well as the app shell, and the app area on a classic page sits in its own panel so the theme does not bleed into the rest of the site.
  • Improved: an expired quote or invoice link counts its privacy window from the last time the document was sent, not from the day it was created, so “send it again” makes the link work again. The expired page says so.
  • Improved: the year report splits “Labor, employees” from “Contract labor” and adds a “tax collected, by rate” table on a cash basis, next to the accrual “Tax Billed” tile, with a note saying which is which.
  • Improved: the browser tab is titled after the screen (“Customer History #10, Acme Painting”) instead of the page name, on every layout.
  • Improved: a painter adding a receipt sees the amount of their own earlier receipts on the job and not a colleague’s.
  • Improved: on an iPhone the install hint says where Add to Home Screen lives, and going offline no longer stacks a second banner on top of the first.
  • Fixed: the job-start reminder read “begins tomorrow, the 30th at .” when the job had no start time.
  • Fixed: a stray table cell on the vehicle settings page.
  • Fixed: the data export now includes a painters CSV, and the quote and invoice files no longer carry the customers’ public link tokens.
  • Fixed: two upgrade steps read a column’s type through information_schema, which answers nothing on some MySQL 8 hosts, so the step was skipped there without a word: the photo attachment column could stay NOT NULL (every AI render save would then fail), and this version’s quote-cents widening would not have run. Both now read the type with SHOW COLUMNS, the same way the rest of the upgrader does.

1.2.063

  • Fixed: on a site that installed PaintClarity fresh from 1.2.059 on, business expenses and vehicle trips were reported as saved and were not. Two of the plugin’s tables were never created because a note inside their definition contained a semicolon. The tables are created on upgrade, and a save that fails now says so instead of showing a green notice.
  • Fixed: an invoice raised for the remaining balance was shown to the customer with the job’s earlier payments subtracted a second time, so a $2,493 invoice after a $1,000 deposit read “Balance Due $1,493.00” and the online payment charged that. An invoice now remembers what had been paid when it was raised, and only money received after that reduces it. A second invoice on a job keeps its own amount after the first one is paid.
  • Fixed: editing a job and saving without touching the tax box could quietly move it to today’s default rate when the rate it was stamped with had been changed or retired, which restated a quote that was already out. A stamped job keeps its rate unless you pick a different one; the form now shows a rate that is no longer offered and says so.
  • Fixed: a painter given “view financials” could open the Business page, the Checkup, the Expenses page, the year-end reports and any job’s profit coversheet, including the hourly rates of the whole crew. That permission now covers the painter’s own jobs only; the office pages and reports are for staff.
  • Fixed: a check-in or check-out saved on the phone while out of signal could be dropped without a word if the app had been open more than a day. Saved punches are now kept until they send, the app fetches a fresh key before sending, and it tells the painter when something is still waiting.
  • Fixed: when a customer signed a quote and the online deposit could not start, they were shown a technical error and the same form again while their signature and any add-on they ticked were already recorded. The acceptance is now completed the same way an offline acceptance is, the customer is thanked and told you will arrange the deposit, and your email says what went wrong on the Stripe side.
  • Fixed: the itemized quote a customer signs listed an accepted add-on twice, once at its price and once at your internal cost. The cost line stays in your own costing and never prints for the customer.
  • Invoices now state the tax included, the rate, and the amount before tax, matching the quote to the cent.
  • The public quote says how the deposit is paid when it is not collected online, and the deposit percentage prints as the tier you set (35%) rather than a recomputed 34.98%.
  • The invoice email only promises “pay online” when the page will have a Pay button, and it goes out from your company address like the quote does.
  • A customer opening, signing, or declining a quote, and a deposit paid online, now appear in the job’s Message History.
  • Every customer-facing dead end (an expired quote, a link that no longer works, a decline) now shows your company name, phone and email.
  • Checkup’s “Create invoice” link opens the job’s Financials invoices, not “Invoice not found”.
  • Creating a request no longer leaves the form filled in under the success message, which made a second click create a duplicate.
  • A painter’s home screen lists a multi-day job under Today for every day it runs, not under Needs attention from day two.
  • Checking in on a job while still checked in on another now checks you out of the first one at that moment and says so, instead of paying both.
  • The before/after comparison slider had its labels the wrong way round; Before is on the left.
  • The mileage rate accepts half cents (the IRS rate for 2026 is 72.5 cents) and the settings text says which year is which.
  • Imported quotes that carry a tax figure now stamp the job with the rate that figure implies, so Financials and the quote agree.
  • New (Pro): AI Visualizer, a second tab on the Visualizer. Upload or take a photo, pick colors by brand and name from the Sherwin-Williams and Benjamin Moore books, add notes like “paint the stone wall too, in Alabaster”, and get back a repainted photo to show the customer. Uses your own OpenAI key (Settings > AI, with a new image model, quality and monthly cap). Renders can be saved to the job’s photos. The Manual tab is unchanged and still runs entirely in your browser.
  • The AI Visualizer answers the browser as soon as the render is handed to OpenAI and then checks back for the result, so a web host or proxy that cuts off long requests no longer ends a render with “did not come back”. Settings > AI shows a record of the last render, including one the host stopped.
  • The primary figure on stat tiles (Profit, Request Acceptance Rate) no longer carries a blue rule across its top; every tile is the same plain card.
  • The More Actions tile on a job keeps its name while open (the chevron shows the state); the longer “Hide” label used to wrap and stretch every tile beside it. Same on the quote and invoice views.
  • The remove button on an AI Visualizer color row has a proper touch target and breathing room from the card edge.
  • AI Visualizer renders ask OpenAI for its less restrictive image filter and describe the photo as a building for a painting estimate, after the default filter rejected an ordinary house front as unsafe. A rejection that still happens explains itself and says what to try.
  • Housekeeping: the database schema and the default content data moved out of the main plugin file into includes, keeping it well inside the size limit that produced a broken Pro update in 1.2.019. No behavior change.

1.2.060

  • New: bring your customers in from a spreadsheet. Settings > Import takes a CSV out of your old system, a phone’s contact export or a list you typed yourself. It shows you exactly what it read before anything is saved, and tells you which rows it would skip and why. Nothing is written until you press the button on the second screen.
  • The import matches on email first, then on phone number, then on an exact name. A row that could be two different customers you already have is skipped and listed for you, never merged on a guess. If the result is not what you wanted, Undo removes only the records that import created and leaves everything else alone.
  • New: bring in past jobs and quotes as well, on the same screen. Old records and a new system rarely line up, so you say what you are loading: finished history, which lands as completed work, or open work you are still chasing. A job whose customer is not on file yet gets that customer created along with it.
  • A fresh install can start over. “Delete all data and import” clears what PaintClarity holds and loads the file cleanly, which is what you want the second time you try an export you have since fixed. “Merge with existing records” is the default and never deletes anything.
  • Fixed: a customer who paid you more than the billable amount looked exactly like a customer who had paid to the penny. A $400 job settled with $480 now says …

short_description: Run your painting business from WordPress: quotes to invoices, crews, scheduling, customers, photos, profit reports, optional AI and card payments.
description:
PaintClarity turns your WordPress site into the back office for your painting business. (PaintClarity was formerly known as PaintOps. Same plugin, same team, same data.) Build professional quotes, send them to customers who can view, e-sign, and pay a deposit online, schedule crews on a calendar, track every job from lead to invoice, and, on Pro, see your real profit per job, per crew, and per worker.

It was built by a painter, for painters. The quote builder understands painting scope: interior/exterior components, standard inclusions and exclusions, and the disclaimer language that keeps you out of disputes. Your data lives in your own WordPress database, not locked inside someone else’s SaaS.

Quote to invoice, start to finish

  • Quotes, estimates & bids: a scope-aware builder with reusable inclusions/exclusions, itemized or lump-sum pricing, printable output, and email delivery.
  • A professional customer page: your customer opens a clean, branded page (your logo, your terms & conditions) and accepts by typing their name, an e-signature-grade record with timestamp. They can also decline with a reason, or ask a question, and you’re notified either way.
  • Acceptance converts the quote to a job automatically, whether they paid a deposit online or you shook hands, and a “Mark as Won” button covers the phone call.
  • Invoices: numbered invoices for the balance (full or partial), emailed or shared by link, payable online (Pro + Stripe) or marked paid for check/cash, with the payment logged so balances always agree.
  • Receivables at a glance: unpaid invoices surface on your dashboard with amounts and age.

Running the work

  • Scheduling calendar with crew filtering, worker badges, time-off, and a subscribe link for Google/Apple/Outlook. Add your own recurring holiday labels.
  • Crews: group your painters into named, colored crews; staff a job with one tap and filter the calendar and reports by crew.
  • Job board / pipeline: Quote → Active → Completed, plus a lost-leads drawer with the customer’s decline reason so you can revive the ones worth re-working.
  • A real app for your painters: install-to-home-screen (PWA), a “My Jobs” home, one-tap directions (Google/Apple/Waze), per-job check-in/out that works offline and syncs, photo/receipt/note logging, a “My Hours” view of their own time and pay, and a “Mark Job Complete” button that notifies the office. Workers see only what their permissions allow, never your numbers.
  • Customers: a directory with contact details, lifetime value, job history, and multiple service addresses per customer, built for landlords, realtors, property managers, and GCs whose one account means a dozen properties.
  • Before/After photos with camera alignment overlay and a compare slider.
  • Color Visualizer: load a photo of the house or the room, select the surface, and turn a color wheel until it is the color you are proposing. The wall changes color and keeps its own shading, grain and texture. Select by fill, by matching color, or by dragging a box over a big flat wall. Handles stucco, siding, brick, concrete block and interior drywall, takes the Sherwin-Williams or Benjamin Moore number alongside it, and prints or saves the render for the customer. The Manual tab runs entirely in your browser: no photo is uploaded anywhere.
  • AI Visualizer (Pro): the other tab. Upload or take a photo, pick colors by brand and name from the Sherwin-Williams and Benjamin Moore books, add a note like “paint the stone wall too, in Alabaster”, and get back a realistic repainted photo to show the customer. This tab sends the photo to OpenAI under your own API key (Settings > AI), billed to your OpenAI account at a few cents per render. Renders can be saved to the job’s photos. Colors on screen are approximate; brand and color names are trademarks of their owners and PaintClarity is not affiliated with any paint manufacturer.
  • Trade calculators, paint-color tracking, and resource links.
  • A choice of visual themes (light, dark, industrial, and more) with a modern app-style navigation bar on desktop and phone.

What Pro adds

  • Job financials & profitability: costs, materials, labor hours; gross, expenses, profit, and margin per job; a Profits dashboard with profit-by-classification, profit-per-hour rankings, and profit by crew and by worker (allocated by logged hours).
  • Expenses & receipts against any job, plus business-level and vehicle expense tracking for tax time.
  • Online payments: deposits on quote acceptance and invoice balances through Stripe Checkout, recorded automatically.
  • AI tools (bring your own OpenAI key): estimate dimensions, gallons, and a Description of Work from a photo; scan receipts to auto-fill expenses; get feedback on or a rewrite of your quote wording.

Pro is a paid upgrade handled through Freemius. The free plugin is fully functional on its own; Pro is optional.

Bundled artwork

The four ready-made logos offered under Business > Logo URL (assets/img/logos/) are AI-generated original artwork created for this plugin. They carry no third-party rights and are distributed under the same GPLv2-or-later license as the rest of the plugin. They are optional, off by default, and carry no PaintClarity branding or link.

External services

This plugin can connect to the following third-party services. Some are optional and only run when you enable and configure the corresponding feature.

OpenAI (Pro AI features, optional). When you use an AI feature (Photo Estimate, Receipt Scan, Description-of-Work Feedback or Rewrite), the plugin sends the relevant input, the photo you choose to upload and/or the quote text you are working on, to the OpenAI API using your own OpenAI API key, and receives the generated result. No data is sent unless you click one of these buttons. PaintClarity does not store the photo. Requests go to https://api.openai.com. See OpenAI’s Terms (https://openai.com/policies/terms-of-use) and Privacy Policy (https://openai.com/policies/privacy-policy).

Stripe (Pro online payments, optional). If you enable card payments and a customer pays online, the plugin creates a Stripe Checkout session and verifies Stripe’s webhook using your own Stripe keys. Order/amount details are exchanged with Stripe to process the payment. Requests go to https://api.stripe.com. See Stripe’s Services Agreement (https://stripe.com/legal/ssa) and Privacy Policy (https://stripe.com/privacy).

Google Maps Platform (optional). If you add a Google Maps API key, address fields use Google Places/Geocoding for autocomplete and validation, and job locations may be shown on an embedded map. The address text you type is sent to Google to return suggestions. Requests go to https://maps.googleapis.com and related Google Maps endpoints. See Google’s Terms (https://cloud.google.com/maps-platform/terms) and Privacy Policy (https://policies.google.com/privacy). (One-tap turn-by-turn Directions for your crew use keyless map links and need no API key.)

YouTube and Vimeo (Resources page video embeds, optional). The Resources page (staff-facing, inside your admin area) lets you save links to training videos, and seeds a starter list of publicly available painting tutorials on YouTube. When a staff member clicks a saved YouTube or Vimeo link’s play button, the video is embedded on the page via the provider’s standard embed player (www.youtube.com / player.vimeo.com), which loads content from that provider and is subject to its terms; no data is sent until the play button is clicked, and you can delete any or all saved links. See YouTube’s Terms (https://www.youtube.com/t/terms) and Google’s Privacy Policy (https://policies.google.com/privacy), and Vimeo’s Terms (https://vimeo.com/terms) and Privacy Policy (https://vimeo.com/privacy).

Freemius (licensing & updates). PaintClarity uses the Freemius SDK to manage Pro licenses, deliver Pro updates, and (optionally) collect anonymous usage diagnostics you can opt out of. Site and license information is exchanged with Freemius. See Freemius’s Terms (https://freemius.com/terms/) and Privacy Policy (https://freemius.com/privacy/).

You control every one of these by whether you enter the corresponding API key and enable the feature. With no keys entered, PaintClarity runs entirely on your own site.

Privacy

Your customers’ details live in your own WordPress database. PaintClarity’s author never sees them, and nothing is sent to a PaintClarity server. That also means you, not the plugin, are the one a customer asks when they want to know what you hold about them, so the plugin’s job is to make sure you can answer.

Quote and invoice pages are blocked from search engines. Those pages are reached by a long private link rather than a password, and a link can be forwarded, pasted into a chat, or picked up from a referrer header. Every customer-facing document PaintClarity serves is marked no-index, no-archive at both the page and the header level, so a link that escapes cannot turn into a search result.

Data requests work out of the box. Under Tools -> Export Personal Data and Tools -> Erase Personal Data, WordPress can search PaintClarity by email address. Export collects the customer record, their jobs, quotes, invoices, payments, and the emails you sent them. Erase removes their details from all of it.

Erasing does not destroy your books. Quotes, invoices and payments are kept and stripped of the name, address, phone, email, typed signature and IP address instead of being deleted, because a business is required to keep financial records for years and data protection law allows exactly that. Any quote or invoice link previously sent to that customer stops working. Job photos are left for you to review yourself rather than deleted automatically.

Suggested privacy policy wording for what PaintClarity stores and which services can receive data is added to Settings -> Privacy -> Policy Guide.

Three optional limits, all off by default, under PaintClarity -> Settings -> Privacy & Customer Data: delete the emailed-communication log after N months, forget the IP address recorded when a quote was signed online after N months, and make quote and invoice links stop working after N days. A business working only in the United States can leave all three off and nothing changes.

None of this is Pro. It is all in the free plugin.
